info.name: Yuno Payments API
info.description:
Yuno is a payment orchestration platform that connects merchants to multiple
payment providers through a single API. Process payments, manage customers,
handle subscriptions, and disburse payouts across Latin America, Asia, and beyond.

## Quick start
1. Import this collection and the **Yuno Sandbox** environment.
2. Set `public_api_key`, `private_secret_key` and `account_id` in the environment.
3. Open **Start here: your first payment** and send the requests in order.

## How it works
- **Same structure as the API reference.** Folders and requests follow the sidebar on docs.y.uno, and every request links to its page.
- **Auth is wired.** `public-api-key` and `private-secret-key` read from the environment. Never commit or share an environment with keys in it.
- **Idempotency is automatic.** `X-Idempotency-Key` gets a fresh UUID on every send, saved as `last_idempotency_key`. When a request times out and you do not know its outcome, copy that value into `retry_idempotency_key` and send again: Yuno returns the original result instead of creating a second payment. Clear `retry_idempotency_key` afterwards.
- **IDs chain.** A successful create saves its ID (`customer_id`, `payment_id`, ...) as a collection variable, and later requests use it.
- **Every documented scenario is a saved example.** Open the examples under a request to see each body and its response.
- **Errors are explained.** A failed call prints the error code, messages and trace ID in the Postman console.

## Environments
- Sandbox: `https://api-sandbox.y.uno/v1`
- Production: `https://api.y.uno/v1` (real money)

This collection is generated from the Yuno OpenAPI spec, so it always matches the API reference.

- API reference: https://docs.y.uno/reference/getting-started/api-reference-overview
- OpenAPI spec: https://docs.y.uno/openapi.json
- Postman guide: https://docs.y.uno/reference/getting-started/postman-collections

item.name: Start here: your first payment
item.description:
Five requests that take you from zero to a refunded sandbox payment. Send them in order, or run the folder.

Before you send:
1. Import and select the **Yuno Sandbox** environment.
2. Fill in `public_api_key`, `private_secret_key` and `account_id` from the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.y.uno/developers), with the context chip on **Test**.
3. Make sure the account can process cards: connect the Yuno Testing Gateway and route cards to it (https://docs.y.uno/docs/direct-integration-use-cases/yuno-testing-gateway). Without a card route, step 3 fails.

Each request saves the IDs the next one needs (`customer_id`, `checkout_session`, `payment_id`, `transaction_id`), so you never copy and paste.

Guide: https://docs.y.uno/reference/getting-started/postman-collections

header.description: Public API key from Dashboard > Settings > API Keys
Private secret key (server-side only)
Required only for organizations with multiple accounts. Identifies which account to use for the request.
Optional client key, up to 64 characters. Best-effort; re-sending the same key is not guaranteed to be de-duplicated.

request.description:
Creates a new custom checkout as a published clone of the account's default checkout: payment methods (including icon/name overrides and required-field condition sets) are copied from the default; general settings and styling inherit the account baseline until the checkout's first publish. The new checkout is born with status PUBLISHED and is never the account's default. The identifier is exposed as the top-level `id`.

request.description:
Renames, publishes, unpublishes, archives, restores, or promotes the checkout. The body carries any combination of `name`, `description`, `status`, and `is_default`; at least one field is required (an empty body is rejected with 400). Status transitions follow the lifecycle state machine: publish (`PUBLISHED`) is only valid from `NOT_PUBLISHED`; an ARCHIVED checkout is restored in two steps (`status: NOT_PUBLISHED` first, then `status: PUBLISHED`); patching to the current status is rejected. Metadata (`name`/`description`) remains editable while ARCHIVED. `is_default` accepts only `true`: it promotes the checkout to account default, force-publishing it from any state, and atomically demotes the previous default; when `is_default: true` is sent together with `status`, the promotion wins and `status` is ignored. The default checkout cannot be archived or unpublished.

Docs: https://docs.y.uno/reference/checkout-builder/manage-checkout-lifecycle

item.name: PCI Proxy

header.description: Public API key from Dashboard > Settings > API Keys
Private secret key (server-side only)

The complete destination URL, including its path and any query string (for example `https://api.example-processor.com/charges/ch_123/capture?expand=true`). Must be a public HTTPS hostname on port 443, and the host must be registered on your destination allowlist; IP addresses and internal networks are rejected. It must not contain `{{vaulted_token...}}` expressions (card data must never appear in a URL).
Destination timeout in seconds. Default 30, maximum 120.

Optional account scope. Narrows which allowlisted destinations are permitted for this request; it does not affect token resolution (vaulted tokens are always scoped to your organization). Like all `yuno-*` headers it is removed before forwarding and never reaches the destination.

Signing scheme for destinations that require HMAC request signing over the body. The proxy computes the signature over the resolved body (after expression substitution) and injects the destination's auth headers; your signing secret is used in memory and discarded — nothing is stored. Supported: `DLOCAL_HMAC` (the proxy generates `X-Date` and computes `Authorization: V2-HMAC-SHA256, Signature: <hex>` over `X-Login + X-Date + resolved body`; you send `X-Login`, `X-Trans-Key`, and `X-Version` as normal destination headers). An unknown value — or a `DLOCAL_HMAC` request missing the `X-Login` or `X-Trans-Key` headers — is rejected with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` before the destination is contacted.
Your signing secret for this request (required when `yuno-proxy-auth` is present). Like every `yuno-*` header it is stripped before forwarding and excluded from logs.

request.description:
Forwards your request to the destination indicated in the `yuno-proxy-destination-url` header, replacing `{{vaulted_token.<TOKEN>.<field>}}` expressions in the body and header values with real card data inside Yuno's PCI DSS Level 1 environment. The destination's status code, headers, and body are returned unchanged. `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` are also supported and forwarded verbatim. The full destination (including its path and query string) is specified in `yuno-proxy-destination-url`; a query string on the `/pci-proxy/forward` request itself is rejected. Every proxy response carries a `yuno-proxy-request-id` header; a `401` returned before the request reaches the proxy is the only exception.

Docs: https://docs.y.uno/reference/pci-proxy/invoke-forward-proxy

item.description:

Guides and object references for this section:

item.name: Update the split of a paid transaction

header.description: Public API key from Dashboard > Settings > API Keys
Private secret key (server-side only)

Required. Unique identifier of this update (MAX 64). A request that times out is not a failure: repeat it with the same key and you get the outcome of the first attempt. The same key with a different body is refused with `SPLIT_UPDATE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. A repeat sent while the first attempt is still running is answered `400` `OPERATION_IN_PROCESS` and changes nothing: wait a few seconds and repeat it again with the same key.

variable.description: The unique identifier of the payment (MAX 64; MIN 36).
The unique identifier of the purchase transaction whose split is replaced (MAX 64; MIN 36).

request.description:
Replaces the whole `split_marketplace` of a succeeded purchase transaction at the provider and in Yuno. The legs sent become the split; legs that are not sent are removed. The payment and the transaction keep their status; no new transaction is created.

The update is accepted only while the provider still allows it: before settlement, and while the payment has no refund (including one waiting to be retried), chargeback or transfer reversal. While an update is in progress or under review, refunds of the payment are refused with `400` `OPERATION_IN_PROCESS`. Availability depends on the provider; contact Yuno to enable it for your connection.

Docs: https://docs.y.uno/reference/recipients-for-marketplace/update-split-marketplace

request.description:
Moves a subscription onto a subscription plan.

If the subscription is not on a plan yet, it is attached in place and keeps its `id`. If it is already on a plan, it is canceled and replaced by a **new** subscription on the target plan; the response is the replacement, and its `previous_subscription_id` points at the subscription it replaced.

In both cases the change takes effect at the subscription's **next renewal** — no charge is made now and nothing is prorated or refunded.

Docs: https://docs.y.uno/reference/subscriptions/change-subscription-plan

request.description:
Moves an external subscription (a Stripe Billing subscription linked through the billing bridge) to another payment method the customer already enrolled in Yuno, without a payment.

No payment is made: Yuno does not charge the customer and does not run a $0 verification or 3DS. The next renewals charge the new payment method.

`customer_payer.id` is the Yuno customer ID, not the Stripe customer ID (`cus_...`). Sending the payment method the subscription already charges returns `200` and changes nothing.

This API is enabled per account: contact your Key Account Manager to request access.

Docs: https://docs.y.uno/reference/subscriptions/change-external-subscription-payment-method

request.description:
Updates an account group. Every field is optional and only the fields present in the body are changed.

`parent_code` nests the group under another group of the same organization. It has three states: **absent** leaves the current parent untouched; **`null`** detaches the group and promotes it back to a root, together with any sub-groups hanging off it; a **group `id`** nests the group under that group. Nesting is structural only — it grants and revokes nothing, so moving a group leaves every existing permission untouched.

Docs: https://docs.y.uno/reference/organizations/update-account-group

request.description:
Stores your own connection instructions for this provider, replacing the Yuno catalogue's wording where you override it.

The document is stored whole, not merged. A field this body omits is cleared, and the provider reverts to the catalogue value for it — so read the current document with `GET`, edit it, and put the whole thing back. At least one of `instructions`, `setup_instructions`, `more_info_url` and `name` must be present, unknown top-level keys are rejected rather than ignored, and the serialised document may not exceed 64 KB.

Every `link`, and `more_info_url`, must be https. `name` renames the provider and is accepted only for Yuno-owned providers (a catalogue id containing `YUNO`); any other provider is rejected with `400`. Rejections list every violation at once in `violations`.

request.description:
Uploads your own logo for this provider. The image travels base64 in JSON, not multipart.

A logo is the provider's identity rather than its wording, so it is held to the same rule as `name`: accepted only for Yuno-owned providers (a catalogue id containing `YUNO`) and rejected with `400` for anyone else's. The file must be a PNG or a JPEG — decided by the file's own bytes, never by the extension, so an SVG renamed `.png` is refused — and square, at least 200x200 pixels and at most 64 KB decoded. Rejections list every violation at once in `violations`.

The stored key is not returned: read the provider again for a fresh presigned `logo_url`. Writing a logo does not touch the instruction override, and does not add the provider to your allowlist.

Docs: https://docs.y.uno/reference/organizations/whitelabel/upload-provider-logo

exec: // Runs before every request in the collection.
// v2 endpoints live on the same host as v1.
// Idempotency: a new key on every send. When a request times out and you do
// not know its outcome, set retry_idempotency_key to last_idempotency_key and
// send again: Yuno returns the original result and never charges twice.
// Only a request that sends the header updates last_idempotency_key, so a
// lookup in between never replaces the key of the request you want to retry.
if (retryKey && sendsKey) console.warn("Yuno: reusing X-Idempotency-Key " + retryKey + " (retry_idempotency_key is set).");
throw new Error("Yuno: " + missing.join(" and ") + " not set. Select the Yuno Sandbox environment and paste your API keys from https://dashboard.y.uno/developers");
// Sandbox keys only work on api-sandbox.y.uno, live keys only on api.y.uno.
if (sandboxHost && /^prod/i.test(publicKey)) console.warn("Yuno: you are sending a production key to the sandbox host.");
if (!sandboxHost && /^sandbox/i.test(publicKey)) console.warn("Yuno: you are sending a sandbox key to the production host.");
if (!sandboxHost) console.warn("Yuno: this request goes to PRODUCTION (" + baseUrl + ").");
// Runs after every request in the collection.
if (trace) console.error("Yuno trace id (send this to support): " + trace);
